Statement: For every integer $k\ge1$ and $\varepsilon>0$, every sufficiently high-dimensional real normed space contains a $k$-dimensional subspace whose Banach–Mazur distance from $\ell_2^k$ is at most $1+\varepsilon$.
Notes: Almost Euclidean sections in every sufficiently large dimension. The date is the full 1961 proceedings paper; Dvoretzky had announced the result in PNAS in 1959. The symposium itself was in 1960.
Source: Dvoretzky, Some results on convex bodies and Banach spaces, Proc. Internat. Sympos. Linear Spaces (Jerusalem, 1960), 1961, pp. 123–160. https://www.mathnet.ru/php/archive.phtml?jrnid=mat&option_lang=eng&paperid=296&wshow=paper ; Earlier announcement: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC222539/

Statement: For a convex body $K\subset\mathbb R^2$ with $0\in\operatorname{int}K$, its polar satisfies $|K|\,|K^\circ|\ge27/4$. If $K=-K$, the stronger bound is $8$.
Date event: Planar theorem; volume year and conventional date differ
Notes: This is the two-dimensional theorem. Here $K^\circ=\{y:\langle x,y\rangle\le1\text{ for all }x\in K\}$. Mahler’s archive lists the paper under 1939 but gives volume year 1938; sorting uses 1939. Equality characterizations were completed in later work.
Source: Mahler, Ein Minimalproblem für konvexe Polygone, Mathematica B 7 (1938), 118–127, listed under 1939: https://carmamaths.org/resources/mahler/collected.html ; original scan: https://carmamaths.org/resources/mahler/docs/059.pdf ; modern statement: https://arxiv.org/abs/1507.01481

Statement: For convex bodies $K,L,K_3,\ldots,K_n\subset\mathbb R^n$, $n\ge2$, their mixed volumes obey $$V(K,L,K_3,\ldots,K_n)^2\ge V(K,K,K_3,\ldots,K_n)\,V(L,L,K_3,\ldots,K_n).$$
Date event: Alexandrov’s published proof; Fenchel announced it in 1936
Notes: Mixed volume is normalized by $V(K[n])=|K|$. The 1937 date refers to Alexandrov’s published proof. Fenchel announced the inequality in 1936. Either surname counts for the naming bonus.
Source: Alexandrov, Zur Theorie der gemischten Volumina von konvexen Körpern II, Mat. Sbornik 2(44):6 (1937), 1205–1238: https://www.mathnet.ru/eng/sm5648 ; Fenchel, C. R. Acad. Sci. Paris 203 (1936), 764–766.

Statement: For a convex body $K\subset\mathbb R^n$ and integer $0\le j\le n$, $$V(K[j],-K[n-j])\le\binom{n}{j}|K|.$$ Here $K[j]$ means $j$ copies of $K$ in the mixed volume.
Notes: The July 2026 preprint proves Godbersen’s 1938 conjectured inequality and the simplex equality characterization among polytopes. An October 2026 preprint by Fryš, Kotrbatý, Mouamine and Wang treats equality for all convex bodies. This card dates a preprint, not a journal publication.
Source: Kotrbatý–Mouamine, Godbersen’s conjecture and the L_p-Rogers-Shephard inequality, arXiv:2607.20387 (22 July 2026): https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.20387 ; equality extension: https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.06806 ; historical formulation: https://academic.oup.com/imrn/article/2025/22/rnaf341/8322708 ; author’s preprint list: https://karlin.mff.cuni.cz/~kotrbaty/research.html

Statement: A rectifiable simple closed plane curve of length $L$ enclosing area $A$ satisfies $L^2\ge4\pi A$, with equality precisely for a circle.
Notes: The classical inequality is much older. This card dates Hurwitz’s Fourier-method proof, not the first solution or the origin of the problem. Among curves enclosing a fixed area, the circle has the least perimeter.
Source: Hurwitz, Sur quelques applications géométriques des séries de Fourier, Ann. Sci. École Norm. Sup. 19 (1902), 357–408: https://www.numdam.org/articles/10.24033/asens.514/

Statement: If $s(K)$ is the Santaló point of a convex body $K\subset\mathbb R^n$, then $$|K|\,|(K-s(K))^\circ|\le |B_2^n|^2.$$ Ellipsoids attain equality.
Notes: The Santaló point minimizes $|(K-x)^\circ|$ over interior points $x$; $B_2^n$ is the Euclidean unit ball. Blaschke proved the low-dimensional cases in 1917. The general only-if equality characterization is later (Petty, 1985). Blaschke also counts for the naming bonus.
Source: Santaló, Un invariante afín para los cuerpos convexos del espacio de n dimensiones, Portugaliae Math. 8 (1949), 155–161. Author archive: https://fonsespecials.udg.edu/lluis-santalo/el-fons/ ; later research reference: https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/mathematika/article/abs/santalo-point-of-a-function-and-a-functional-form-of-the-santalo-inequality/15E6651DC1E90ECC1A16DAB1DC2A8020

Statement: There is a universal constant $c>0$ such that every convex body $K\subset\mathbb R^n$ of volume $1$ has a hyperplane section of $(n-1)$-dimensional volume at least $c$.
Date event: GAFA publication; preprint appeared in December 2024
Notes: The constant is independent of both the dimension and the body. Klartag and Lehec completed the affirmative resolution using Guan’s bound. Bourgain posed the problem. The first preprint was posted on 19 December 2024; this card uses the 2025 journal date.
Source: Klartag–Lehec, Affirmative Resolution of Bourgain’s Slicing Problem Using Guan’s Bound, Geom. Funct. Anal. 35 (2025), 1147–1168: https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s00039-025-00718-w ; preprint: https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.15044

Statement: For every convex body $K\subset\mathbb R^n$, $$|K-K|\le\binom{2n}{n}|K|,$$ with equality precisely when $K$ is a simplex.
Credited people: Claude Ambrose Rogers / Geoffrey Colin Shephard
Notes: The difference body is $K-K=\{x-y:x,y\in K\}$. It is always centrally symmetric. The inequality gives a sharp upper bound for its volume relative to that of $K$.
Source: Rogers–Shephard, The difference body of a convex body, Archiv der Mathematik 8 (1957), 220–233: https://doi.org/10.1007/BF01899997

Statement: Every convex body $K\subset\mathbb R^n$ has a unique maximum-volume inscribed ellipsoid $E$, centered at $c$, with $E\subset K\subset c+n(E-c)$. For centrally symmetric $K$, $n$ improves to $\sqrt n$.
Notes: A convex body is a compact convex set with nonempty interior. After an affine change of coordinates, its largest inscribed ellipsoid becomes the unit ball. The factors n and square root of n are sharp.
Source: John, Extremum problems with inequalities as subsidiary conditions, Courant Anniversary Volume (1948), 187–204. Later collected-paper reprint: https://doi.org/10.1007/978-1-4612-5412-6_25
